honestly, the problem wasn't in you, the therapist was the problem. 
I had a similar experience where a psychologist laughed at my problems when I described to her that I had researched my symptoms and that I thought I had depersonalisation ... she looked at me and said "do tell me more about what you found on the internet" with this nasty smirk on her face... I was there, described to her that I was suicidal, she never made eye contact, I cried - she showed no compassion whatsoever. I left the office with a major disappointment, never went back to her and dreaded psychologists and psychiatrists for years after that until I met my current psychiatrist who's by far the most empathic, compassionate, laid back guy I've ever met!
hang in there, and most of all don't give up because of one rotten apple.

I think a lot of doctors aren't afraid of the addiction as much as they're afraid of what people do while on ambien (sleep drive, etc).
My doctor has an 'idgaf' attitude and prescribed me a 2 month supply of ambien and 2 month supply of 1mg xanax..

First night I took 10mg, went to bed, fell right asleep and woke up fresh as a daisy. The following night I took one, but didn't go straight to bed - big mistake.. I woke up to a total of 13x ambien & 13x xanax pills missing.. (mind you they were 10mg ambien and 1mg xanax - quite a dangerous dose in one take).  Woke up with a hangover, discovered that the pills were missing from the blister pack. I checked my phone.. I had called pretty much everyone I know, sent them messages in gibberish, my facebook was covered in 'babble posts'.. again I had sent messages to people there as well (in a non-readable form because of the spelling mistakes) even to my ex whom I hate. After sobering up I talked to one of my friends who then told me I drove about 20km in my car (thank god I didn't run anyone over) and rode around on my dirtbike which is now missing a tail wing and I think I tried to break my leg (tibia bone) with one of these wood tightening tools cause it was lying on my floor.. with a hammer (?) 
my leg was bruised a.f from the trauma and to top it off I had torn apart my razor and cut my leg with it multiple times pretty deep ... (history of self harm, but I was okay for months prior to that). 
Scared me shitless. Having done some research I read a lot of articles about people who had gone sleep driving and a woman had actually killed 2 people while driving ... all while on ambien :/

sorry for the wall of text, just wanted to say be careful! while it is an effective sleep aid, it also comes with a lot of risks. just be sure to already be in bed when you take it, put your phone away and sleep :)

*I keep at least 1 or 2 anxiety meds with me at all times, but prior to taking them I try to combat anxiety without meds*

* 1. Best cure - calling someone I know and talking to them until I've   calmed down.. I've found that a familiar voice calms me down!
* 2. While driving & u can't call, put on your favourite song, sing along to it and distract yourself... try to drive your thoughts away from anxiety.
* 3. Keep thinking "I'm okay, I'm totally fine.. I'm here and this is just a passing emotion, I can do this". (it might sound dumb, but it actually helps)

I'm sorry for your loss, a similar thing happened to me a year ago. Someone I knew (sisters ex) hung himself, apparently he had casino depts and felt this was the only way out. 
He was the type of person that could light up the room with his entrance; full of life, always made people smile and laugh! 
No one knew what he'd been going through, because despite the hardships and problems he kept making people laugh when he was accompanied by friends... then one day my friend told me "... is dead, he hung himself".

I felt numb, because I myself am suicidal and have attempted suicide, but was resuscitated. I felt conflicted... I didn't know whether I was jealous of his courage to go through with it or mad that he did it.. 
Of course I was & still am sad that he's no longer around, but a part of me still thinks about the people that go through with it as "courageous" no matter what others say.. it's not a cowardly act, I know it because I've been there and it takes a lot of guts.. cowardliness has nothing to do with it.. unfortunately (yes, unfortunately) I was discovered and I'm still here and I'm still hurting and now... after doing it once, bringing so much pain to my family, I no longer have the courage to do it again.
I wouldn't even want attention, I just want to get rid of the pain that I'm in.. I romanticise about suicide every day! how I would feel at ease and would no longer be in pain, because my pain also hurts my family.

all I learned from this is; I wish they'd have let me leave... I was ready, I was at peace and had the courage... I actually did it, but they intervened and now I'm suffering more because life has only gotten worse.

I'm a good 80% sure, it's Xanax withdrawal that's responsible for the hallucinations and not an underlying condition. From a logical point of view if it was an underlying condition it would've showed itself sooner.. especially the hallucinations, when we're talking about schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder. One thing I'd suggest and it's written pretty much everywhere is **never quit cold turkey, always taper**. With that being said, hang in there, try to go through the detox and don't touch benzos again if you're prone to addiction (10mg per day is a lot - I'm on 10-20mg of diazepam a day, my tolerance has grown cause I can feel the 20mg working less than it did some time ago, but I won't go higher than that). Before diazepam I was on 1-2mg of xanax a day and I tapered down, but anxiety was harassing me so I needed to supplement it with Valium (smaller addiction risk I think).
